work.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 1, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. The Duke of Gloucester's House

content.text: Enter Duke Humphrey of Gloucester and his wife Eleanor.

lines.text: Why droops my lord, like over-ripened corn
lines.plainText: Why droops my lord like overripened corn

lines.text: Hanging the head at Ceres' plenteous load?
lines.plainText: Hanging the head at Ceres' plenteous load

lines.text: Why doth the great Duke Humphrey knit his brows,
lines.plainText: Why doth the great Duke Humphrey knit his brows

lines.text: As frowning at the favours of the world?
lines.plainText: As frowning at the favours of the world

lines.text: Why are thine eyes fixed to the sullen earth,
lines.plainText: Why are thine eyes fixed to the sullen earth

lines.text: Gazing on that which seems to dim thy sight?
lines.plainText: Gazing on that which seems to dim thy sight

lines.text: What seest thou there? King Henry's diadem,
lines.plainText: What seest thou there King Henry's diadem

lines.text: Enchased with all the honours of the world?
lines.plainText: Enchased with all the honours of the world

lines.text: If so, gaze on, and grovel on thy face,
lines.plainText: If so gaze on and grovel on thy face

lines.text: Until thy head be circled with the same.
lines.plainText: Until thy head be circled with the same

lines.text: Put forth thy hand, reach at the glorious gold.
lines.plainText: Put forth thy hand reach at the glorious gold

lines.text: What, is't too short? I'll lengthen it with mine;
lines.plainText: What is't too short I'll lengthen it with mine

lines.text: And, having both together heaved it up,
lines.plainText: And having both together heaved it up

lines.text: We'll both together lift our heads to heaven,
lines.plainText: We'll both together lift our heads to heaven

lines.text: And never more abase our sight so low
lines.plainText: And never more abase our sight so low

lines.text: As to vouchsafe one glance unto the ground.
lines.plainText: As to vouchsafe one glance unto the ground

lines.text: O Nell, sweet Nell, if thou dost love thy lord,
lines.plainText: O Nell sweet Nell if thou dost love thy lord

lines.text: Banish the canker of ambitious thoughts.
lines.plainText: Banish the canker of ambitious thoughts

lines.text: And may that hour when I imagine ill
lines.plainText: And may that hour when I imagine ill

lines.text: Against my King and nephew, virtuous Henry,
lines.plainText: Against my King and nephew virtuous Henry

lines.text: Be my last breathing in this mortal world!
lines.plainText: Be my last breathing in this mortal world

lines.text: My troublous dreams this night doth make me sad.
lines.plainText: My troublous dreams this night doth make me sad

lines.text: What dreamed my lord? Tell me, and I'll requite it
lines.plainText: What dreamed my lord Tell me and I'll requite it

lines.text: With sweet rehearsal of my morning's dream.
lines.plainText: With sweet rehearsal of my morning's dream

lines.text: Methought this staff, mine office-badge in court,
lines.plainText: Methought this staff mine officebadge in court

lines.text: Was broke in twain; by whom I have forgot,
lines.plainText: Was broke in twain by whom I have forgot

lines.text: But, as I think, it was by th' Cardinal,
lines.plainText: But as I think it was by th' Cardinal

lines.text: And on the pieces of the broken wand
lines.plainText: And on the pieces of the broken wand

lines.text: Were placed the heads of Edmund, Duke of Somerset
lines.plainText: Were placed the heads of Edmund Duke of Somerset

lines.text: And William de la Pole, first Duke of Suffolk.
lines.plainText: And William de la Pole first Duke of Suffolk

lines.text: This was my dream; what it doth bode, God knows.
lines.plainText: This was my dream what it doth bode God knows

lines.text: Tut, this was nothing but an argument
lines.plainText: Tut this was nothing but an argument

lines.text: That he that breaks a stick of Gloucester's grove
lines.plainText: That he that breaks a stick of Gloucester's grove

lines.text: Shall lose his head for his presumption.
lines.plainText: Shall lose his head for his presumption

lines.text: But list to me, my Humphrey, my sweet Duke:
lines.plainText: But list to me my Humphrey my sweet Duke

lines.text: Methought I sat in seat of majesty
lines.plainText: Methought I sat in seat of majesty

lines.text: In the cathedral church of Westminster
lines.plainText: In the cathedral church of Westminster

lines.text: And in that chair where kings and queens are crowned,
lines.plainText: And in that chair where kings and queens are crowned

lines.text: Where Henry and Dame Margaret kneeled to me
lines.plainText: Where Henry and Dame Margaret kneeled to me

lines.text: And on my head did set the diadem.
lines.plainText: And on my head did set the diadem

lines.text: Nay, Eleanor, then must I chide outright.
lines.plainText: Nay Eleanor then must I chide outright

lines.text: Presumptuous dame, ill-nurtured Eleanor,
lines.plainText: Presumptuous dame illnurtured Eleanor

lines.text: Art thou not second woman in the realm,
lines.plainText: Art thou not second woman in the realm

lines.text: And the Protector's wife, beloved of him?
lines.plainText: And the Protector's wife beloved of him

lines.text: Hast thou not worldly pleasure at command,
lines.plainText: Hast thou not worldly pleasure at command

lines.text: Above the reach or compass of thy thought?
lines.plainText: Above the reach or compass of thy thought

lines.text: And wilt thou still be hammering treachery
lines.plainText: And wilt thou still be hammering treachery

lines.text: To tumble down thy husband and thyself
lines.plainText: To tumble down thy husband and thyself

lines.text: From top of honour to disgrace's feet?
lines.plainText: From top of honour to disgrace's feet

lines.text: Away from me, and let me hear no more!
lines.plainText: Away from me and let me hear no more

lines.text: What, what, my lord! Are you so choleric
lines.plainText: What what my lord Are you so choleric

lines.text: With Eleanor for telling but her dream?
lines.plainText: With Eleanor for telling but her dream

lines.text: Next time I'll keep my dreams unto myself,
lines.plainText: Next time I'll keep my dreams unto myself

lines.text: And not be checked.
lines.plainText: And not be checked

lines.text: Nay, be not angry, I am pleased again.
lines.plainText: Nay be not angry I am pleased again

lines.text: My Lord Protector, 'tis his highness' pleasure
lines.plainText: My Lord Protector 'tis his highness' pleasure

lines.text: You do prepare to ride unto Saint Albans,
lines.plainText: You do prepare to ride unto Saint Albans

lines.text: Whereas the King and Queen do mean to hawk.
lines.plainText: Whereas the King and Queen do mean to hawk

lines.text: I go. Come, Nell, thou wilt ride with us?
lines.plainText: I go Come Nell thou wilt ride with us

lines.text: Yes, my good lord, I'll follow presently.
lines.plainText: Yes my good lord I'll follow presently

lines.text: Jesus preserve your royal majesty!
lines.plainText: Jesus preserve your royal majesty

lines.text: What sayst thou? Majesty! I am but grace.
lines.plainText: What sayst thou Majesty I am but grace

lines.text: But, by the grace of God, and Hume's advice,
lines.plainText: But by the grace of God and Hume's advice

lines.text: Your grace's title shall be multiplied.
lines.plainText: Your grace's title shall be multiplied

lines.text: What sayst thou, man? Hast thou as yet conferred
lines.plainText: What sayst thou man Hast thou as yet conferred

lines.text: With Margery Jourdain, the cunning witch,
lines.plainText: With Margery Jourdain the cunning witch

lines.text: With Roger Bolingbroke, the conjurer?
lines.plainText: With Roger Bolingbroke the conjurer

lines.text: And will they undertake to do me good?
lines.plainText: And will they undertake to do me good

lines.text: This they have promised, to show your highness
lines.plainText: This they have promised to show your highness

lines.text: A spirit raised from depth of underground,
lines.plainText: A spirit raised from depth of underground

lines.text: That shall make answer to such questions
lines.plainText: That shall make answer to such questions

lines.text: As by your Grace shall be propounded him.
lines.plainText: As by your Grace shall be propounded him

lines.text: It is enough, I'll think upon the questions.
lines.plainText: It is enough I'll think upon the questions

lines.text: When from Saint Albans we do make return,
lines.plainText: When from Saint Albans we do make return

lines.text: We'll see these things effected to the full.
lines.plainText: We'll see these things effected to the full

lines.text: Here, Hume, take this reward; make merry, man,
lines.plainText: Here Hume take this reward make merry man

lines.text: With thy confederates in this weighty cause.
lines.plainText: With thy confederates in this weighty cause

lines.text: Hume must make merry with the Duchess' gold.
lines.plainText: Hume must make merry with the Duchess' gold

lines.text: Marry, and shall. But, how now, Sir John Hume!
lines.plainText: Marry and shall But how now Sir John Hume

lines.text: Seal up your lips, and give no words but mum;
lines.plainText: Seal up your lips and give no words but mum

lines.text: The business asketh silent secrecy.
lines.plainText: The business asketh silent secrecy

lines.text: Dame Eleanor gives gold to bring the witch;
lines.plainText: Dame Eleanor gives gold to bring the witch

lines.text: Gold cannot come amiss, were she a devil.
lines.plainText: Gold cannot come amiss were she a devil

lines.text: Yet have I gold flies from another coast.
lines.plainText: Yet have I gold flies from another coast

lines.text: I dare not say, from the rich cardinal
lines.plainText: I dare not say from the rich cardinal

lines.text: And from the great and new-made Duke of Suffolk,
lines.plainText: And from the great and newmade Duke of Suffolk

lines.text: Yet I do find it so. For, to be plain,
lines.plainText: Yet I do find it so For to be plain

lines.text: They, knowing Dame Eleanor's aspiring humour,
lines.plainText: They knowing Dame Eleanor's aspiring humour

lines.text: Have hired me to undermine the Duchess
lines.plainText: Have hired me to undermine the Duchess

lines.text: And buzz these conjurations in her brain.
lines.plainText: And buzz these conjurations in her brain

lines.text: They say "A crafty knave does need no broker",
lines.plainText: They say A crafty knave does need no broker

lines.text: Yet am I Suffolk and the cardinal's broker.
lines.plainText: Yet am I Suffolk and the cardinal's broker

lines.text: Hume, if you take not heed, you shall go near
lines.plainText: Hume if you take not heed you shall go near

lines.text: To call them both a pair of crafty knaves.
lines.plainText: To call them both a pair of crafty knaves

lines.text: Well, so its stands; and thus, I fear, at last
lines.plainText: Well so its stands and thus I fear at last

lines.text: Hume's knavery will be the Duchess' wrack,
lines.plainText: Hume's knavery will be the Duchess' wrack

lines.text: And her attainture will be Humphrey's fall.
lines.plainText: And her attainture will be Humphrey's fall

lines.text: Sort how it will, I shall have gold for all.
lines.plainText: Sort how it will I shall have gold for all
